label: articularis genu muscle

is_a.label: muscle organ
is_a.evidence: The articularis genus (also known as the subcrureus muscle) is a small skeletal muscle located anteriorly on the thigh just above the knee.

part_of.label: hindlimb stylopod
part_of.evidence: The articularis genus (also known as the subcrureus muscle) is a small skeletal muscle located anteriorly on the thigh just above the knee.

has_muscle_origin.label: femur
has_muscle_origin.evidence: It arises from the anterior surface of the lower part of the body of the femur, deep to the vastus intermedius, close to the knee and from the deep fibers of the vastus intermedius.

has_muscle_insertion.label: suprapatellar bursa / synovial membrane of knee joint
has_muscle_insertion.evidence: Its insertion is on the synovial membrane of the knee-joint. [Infobox: Insertion: Suprapatellar bursa]
has_muscle_insertion.notes: No clear UBERON term resolved for suprapatellar bursa; left unresolved.

innervated_by.label: femoral nerve
innervated_by.evidence: It is innervated by branches of the femoral nerve (L2-L4).

has_muscle_action.value: pulls the suprapatellar bursa superiorly during extension of the knee, preventing impingement of the synovial membrane between the patella and the femur
has_muscle_action.evidence: Articularis genus pulls the suprapatellar bursa superiorly during extension of the knee, and prevents impingement of the synovial membrane between the patella and the femur.

notes: Articularis genus is a distinct small skeletal muscle of the anterior thigh, often described as separated from but closely associated with vastus intermedius (UBERON:0014847). Insertion field has no resolved UBERON ID because suprapatellar bursa / knee synovial membrane was not found as a discrete UBERON class in OLS lookup; left as a free-text label with evidence quote. Wikipedia evidence is sourced from Grant's Atlas of Anatomy (Agur & Dalley 2009) and Gray's Anatomy (1918) per the article's references.
